steps.say: Rheumatoid nodules indicate seropositive disease with fibrinoid centres. They occur in 20 to 30 percent of patients over pressure points. Histology is palisading histiocytes around central necrosis. Nodules never occur in truly seronegative disease.
steps.tx: Rheumatoid nodules develop in **20 to 30 percent** of rheumatoid arthritis (chronic symmetric joint disease) patients, virtually always seropositive for rheumatoid factor and anti citrullinated antibodies. Histology is central **fibrinoid necrosis** (pink amorphous dead tissue) ringed by palisading CD68 positive epithelioid histiocytes with outer mononuclear cells, typically over extensor pressure points like the olecranon. A nodule in a seronegative patient requires biopsy, because mimics outnumber true nodules there.

steps.say: Lung disease in rheumatoid arthritis is usually UIP with honeycombing. It occurs in 10 percent of patients and carries a poor prognosis. In other connective tissue diseases, NSIP is the predominant pattern. Every breathless RA patient requires a high resolution CT.
steps.tx: Rheumatoid arthritis associated interstitial lung disease (**RA-ILD**, lung scarring) is clinical in **10 percent** of patients. Unlike other connective tissue diseases where non specific interstitial pneumonia dominates, RA presents with usual interstitial pneumonia (**UIP**, patchy basal fibrosis) with subpleural basilar reticulation and **honeycombing** (clustered cystic airspaces) on high resolution CT and histology, carrying poor prognosis. Breathlessness in RA indicates HRCT first, because UIP changes management and prognosis.

steps.say: Felty syndrome is the triad of seropositive arthritis, spleen enlargement, and low neutrophils. Counts below 1000 to 1500 are the definition of the neutropenia. HLA-DR4 and high titre RF are the markers of patients at risk. Recurrent bacterial infections are the clinical clue.
steps.tx: **Felty syndrome** is the triad of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, splenomegaly (enlarged spleen), and severe neutropenia with absolute neutrophil count below **1,000 to 1,500** per microliter. It links to **HLA-DR4** 0401, high titre rheumatoid factor, refractory leg ulcers, and recurrent bacterial infections. Large granular lymphocyte (**LGL**, clonal cytotoxic T cell) leukaemia mimics Felty exactly, with CD3 CD8 CD57 positive cells and **STAT3** mutations above **40 percent**, responding to methotrexate or cyclophosphamide.

steps.say: Rheumatoid vasculitis is a necrotising arteritis of long standing seropositive disease. Ulcers, gangrene, and foot drop are the warning signs. Mortality is high without cyclophosphamide or rituximab. Skin ulcers in RA are never dressed and ignored.
steps.tx: Rheumatoid **vasculitis** (blood vessel wall inflammation) is a severe transmural necrotising small and medium vessel arteritis of long standing seropositive RA. It presents with deep cutaneous ulcerations, digital gangrene, purpura, and **mononeuritis multiplex** (sequential nerve infarcts causing wrist or foot drop), carrying high mortality. Therapy requires **cyclophosphamide** or rituximab with high dose glucocorticoids, because steroids alone cannot control transmural necrosis.

steps.say: Eye disease in RA is a spectrum from dry eyes to globe rupture. Dry eye from secondary Sjogren is the commonest form. Necrotising scleritis threatens vision while scleromalacia perforans is painless. Every red or dry eye in RA requires slit lamp examination.
steps.tx: Ocular disease in RA spans secondary Sjogren **keratoconjunctivitis sicca** (dry eye, commonest), episcleritis, and deep necrotising anterior **scleritis** (painful scleral inflammation). **Scleromalacia perforans** is painless anterior necrosis without inflammation in seropositive nodular RA, thinning the globe toward rupture. Painful red eye indicates scleritis and requires urgent steroids, while a painless blue sclera indicates scleromalacia and requires protection from trivial trauma.

vis.alt: Diagram of episcleral and scleral vascular plexuses with scleral thinning and anterior staphyloma.
vis.caption: Deep scleral inflammation threatens the globe while painless thinning risks rupture from trivial knocks. Slit lamp examination separates them. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The neck is the hidden danger in rheumatoid arthritis. Erosion around the odontoid is the cause of transverse ligament loosening. An interval above 3 mm on flexion views is the definition of subluxation. Flexion films are required before any intubation.
steps.tx: Neck disease in RA centres on the small synovial joints that cradle the **odontoid** (the upward peg of the axis vertebra). Tenosynovitis of the transverse ligament plus peg erosion lets the atlas slide forward. On a flexion lateral film, an anterior atlanto-dens gap beyond **3 mm** is subluxation, and beyond **5 mm** is severe, with cord compression one fall away. Neck pain or neurology in RA requires flexion views first, and intubation never proceeds without clearance.

steps.say: Persistent inflammation produces amyloid that destroys kidneys. Serum amyloid A is driven by IL-6 into glomeruli with nephrotic range proteinuria. Suppressive biologics are the brake on further deposition. Proteinuria in active RA is never assumed benign.
steps.tx: Sustained high grade inflammation drives **AA amyloidosis** (reactive amyloid disease) through IL-6 mediated hepatic overproduction of serum amyloid A. Glomerular deposition causes **nephrotic syndrome** (heavy proteinuria with edema) and progressive renal failure. Suppressive anti IL-6 or anti TNF biologics halt further deposition. New proteinuria in active RA requires amyloid staining of fat or kidney, because early suppression preserves renal function.

vis.alt: Hepatic precursor conversion to amyloid fibrils with glomerular deposition and apple-green birefringence.
vis.caption: Serum amyloid A deposits in glomeruli and shows apple-green birefringence. Suppressive biologics halt the process. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Severe seropositive erosive disease is the predictor of every complication in this lesson. Nodules, lung fibrosis, vasculitis, and amyloid are clustered in the same patients. The deformed hand is the marker of the patient who requires systemic surveillance. The inflammation and the complications are treated together.
steps.tx: Severe seropositive erosive disease predicts the full extra-articular spectrum: nodules in **20 to 30 percent**, UIP lung disease in **10 percent**, vasculitis, scleritis, cervical instability above **3 mm**, and AA amyloidosis. The deformed rheumatoid hand with pannus, erosions, and ulnar drift marks the patient who requires lung, eye, neck, and urine surveillance together. Control inflammation with DMARDs and biologics, because each complication tracks cumulative inflammatory burden.

vis.alt: Synovial hyperplasia with invasive pannus, marginal erosions, and ulnar deviation in rheumatoid arthritis.
vis.caption: Pannus and erosions mark the seropositive burden that predicts lung, eye, neck, and renal complications. Credit: StewardMD.
